chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muthannā ibn Rāshid, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about an orphan who had read the Qur'an, whose intellect had no defect, and who had wealth in the custody of a man. The one holding the wealth wanted to use it productively until he reached puberty and then hand over his wealth to him.
He عليه السلام said: “Even if he reaches puberty, if he does not have sound intellect, nothing should ever be handed over to him.”

key_terms.أَبَدًا: ever; under no circumstance in that condition
key_terms.بِعَقْلِهِ: with respect to his intellect or mental soundness
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: anything at all from the property
key_terms.مَالٌ: wealth or property belonging to the orphan
key_terms.يَتِيمٍ: an orphan, a minor whose property is under protection
key_terms.يَعْمَلَ بِهِ: to use or invest the wealth productively
key_terms.ٱلْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, mentioned here as something the orphan had read

ai.seo_question: When can an orphan’s wealth be handed over to him in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the property of an orphan and the conditions for transferring it to him. It indicates that reaching puberty alone is not sufficient; sound intellect is also required before wealth may be entrusted to the orphan. The report highlights the protection of vulnerable persons and the careful stewardship of financial rights.
